title: de.hubtask.work.item.trashed.v1
description: An entry and everything under it are in the trash: a soft delete waiting out its retention period, reversible until the retention job removes it for good (ADR-0020). Nothing below the entry gets an event of its own - a consumer holding the subtree removes it under the entry's path, the same contract the moved event uses for the same reason (invariant I-W2). Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: A snapshot of the entry as it now stands, with the deletion's own fields: when it went in, which act it belongs to, and how much went with it.

type.description: The level. Extensible by configuration: a consumer that switches on it must tolerate a value it does not know rather than fail (domain-model.md §1).

collection_id.description: The collection the item belongs to. Sent on every level, because the parent alone does not say which collection an item is in until the whole chain has been walked.

parent_id.description: The item above; null for one that sits directly under the collection (invariant I-W1). Sent even when null - it is the parent reference a consumer places the item by, and inferring it from the type would break the day a level is added.

path.description: The materialised path, `/<id>/<id>/…/`, including the item itself and closed by a separator (invariant I-W2).

depth.description: The level below the collection, counting from 1. Bounded by the capability profile of the type.

notes.description: Markdown, unrendered by the server. Absent when unset, and absent on a type whose profile does not carry the NOTES capability.

completion.description: The done/open state. Always sent, though a created item is always open: a rule that reads it should not need a special case for the one event where it happens to be absent.

order_key.description: The rank among the siblings: a fractional index, not a number (offline-sync.md §4.2).

updated_at.description: When the item last changed - the instant of this completion change.

archived_at.description: When the entry was archived: kept, and read-only. Null when it is not. Present on every lifecycle event rather than only on the archiving ones, because an entry can be archived and in the trash at once (domain-model.md §3.4) and a consumer reading one stamp could not tell what state it is now in.

deleted_at.description: When the entry went into the trash. Null when it is not in it. A soft delete with a retention period running against it, not a removal - the entry is still there and can be restored (ADR-0020).

trash_batch_id.description: The deletion every row of one act shares (invariant I-C2). It is what a restore is keyed on, and what tells a consumer that this entry went with something else rather than on its own. Null when the entry is not in the trash.

subtree_size.description: How many rows the act touched, this entry included. A consumer cannot derive it - nothing below the entry gets an event of its own - and it is what tells a client how much of its own copy of the subtree to rewrite.
